subject: Marketplace listing floor, distributor retention & private offer clarifications
messages:
From: Sara Novak <sara@cloudretail.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace listing floor & distributor retention — Private Offer for CloudRetail

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited. We're ready to move to a Private Offer on AWS, but procurement has two asks we need to confirm before we draft the PO:

1) List-price floor / escape: our distributor partner requires a clause that prevents market listing below a negotiated floor for 9 months after the PO is listed (they build marketing and GTM against that list price). Can Redwood include an explicit "listing floor" or an escape clause that triggers buyer notification/fallback pricing?

2) Distributor retention / pass-through: CloudRetail needs assurance that the reseller/distributor will continue to receive an agreed margin (pass-through) even if Redwood issues promotional credits to end-customers. Is there a mechanism in the Private Offer to preserve channel margin or to seed a short-term retention pool (e.g., a 6-month retention credit to distributor)?

3) Pricing cadence: procurement is asking for a clear schedule for allowed promotions/retro credits that won't retroactively clawback partner fees.

I've attached the PO request template and a short note from our procurement team. Happy to hop on a call if easier.

Thanks,
Sara Novak
Head of Procurement, CloudRetail Inc.
Attachments: CloudRetail_PO_Request.docx (docx)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sara Novak <sara@cloudretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing floor & distributor retention — Private Offer for CloudRetail

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Ben (sales ops) and Lauren (partner ops) so we can respond with options. High-level thoughts below; we'll follow up with language suggestions and a draft.

- Listing floor / escape: We can include a listing floor as part of the Private Offer metadata (visible to AWS) and add an "escrow notification" workflow: if Redwood adjusts list price below floor within the protected period, we auto-notify the distributor and optionally route purchases to the fallback SKU (higher-tier listing) for the remainder of the protected window. The 9-month term you asked for is longer than our standard 3–6 month protection; we can make it work but will need to price for the extended risk.

- Distributor retention pool: We have two approaches that customers commonly use: 1) a fixed pass-through percentage on list price (paid to distributor on invoiced revenue) or 2) a short-term retention credit funded out of a small portion of the initial commit (commonly modeled as X% of first 3 months usage reserved for partner retention). Option 2 preserves net economics for Redwood while giving the distributor certainty.

- Promotions & retro credits: We can create a capped promotions cadence in the PO (e.g., max 10% promotional cap per quarter) that is excluded from channel fee adjustments, and we can define an explicit non-clawback window for partner fees.

I've attached a quick workbook with two modeled scenarios (pass-through % vs retention pool) so we can surface the impact on net rev and on distributor margin. Ben/Lauren — can you review and flag preferred default?

Next steps: Ben to run quick margin simulation; Lauren to draft partner-protection language we can insert into the Private Offer; I'll draft a working clause for the listing floor and the escape notification flow.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Exec — Cloud Marketplace, Redwood Inference
Attachments: channel_margin_workbook.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sara Novak <sara@cloudretail.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing floor & distributor retention — Private Offer for CloudRetail

Rafael / Sara — ran the numbers on the two scenarios in the workbook. Quick summary:

- Scenario A (fixed pass-through): 8% pass-through on invoiced list price to distributor. Straightforward, predictable for the partner, but reduces Redwood net rev per unit.
- Scenario B (retention pool): Reserve 3% of forecasted first-quarter usage into a distributor retention pool (paid when partner hits retention milestones). This preserves short-term net rev for Redwood and only pays out if partner maintains agreed activity levels.

Finance is comfortable with Scenario B for a 6-month retention horizon; for 9 months we'd need an elevated reserve (4.5%) or a smaller base discount.

On listing floor language, legal flagged two items we'll need clarified before we propose it to AWS marketplace: 1) what counts as "listing" (public marketplace SKU vs embedded private SKU), and 2) whether the floor is an internal pricing guardrail or a contractual obligation with penalties. If CloudRetail prefers legal penalties for breaches, we should discuss crediting mechanics now.

I uploaded the model and a sensitivity tab here: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-id-channel-margin (drive link).

Action items
- Ben: prepare final numbers for Scenario B with both 6- and 9-month retention windows (due Mon EOW).
- Lauren: draft partner-protection wording for the Private Offer and MSA addendum.
- Rafael: coordinate with Sara on which approach CloudRetail prefers and whether procurement can accept conditional retention (milestone-based) vs guaranteed pass-through.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Novak <sara@cloudretail.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing floor & distributor retention — Private Offer for CloudRetail

Sara — quick legal check and update. We prefer to avoid penalty-based price covenants recorded in the marketplace listing itself; instead, recommend the following hybrid construct which is easier to operationalize with the marketplace:

1) Private Offer metadata includes a 6- or 9-month "protected list price" flag and explicit notification steps for Redwood and the distributor if Redwood proposes a lower list price. The flag is visible to AWS and in the Private Offer record but does not create a third-party enforceable penalty in the marketplace.

2) MSA addendum between Redwood and CloudRetail (attached: pex_terms_redline.pdf) contains the commercial commitment to preserve distributor margin per the agreed pass-through or retention pool mechanics. That addendum is the contractual instrument that creates partner obligations and remedies (non-marketplace).

3) Promotions/retro credits should be governed by a capped cadence clause in the MSA addendum stating that promotional credits up to X% in a rolling quarter do not trigger adjustments to partner fees; any credits beyond that cap are netted against the partner retention pool before any clawback mechanisms.

If CloudRetail wants the 9-month protected list price, we will need to formalize a slightly higher lift on initial pricing (Ben, Rafael — see Ben's sensitivity). Otherwise, 6 months is our standard. Lauren will circulate the addendum redline today; once Sara confirms the preferred protection window we'll surface the DocuSign flow for both the Private Offer and the MSA addendum.

Next steps: Lauren to send redline (cc'ed), Ben to deliver final numbers, Sara to confirm preference (6 vs 9 months). Rafael to own the PO creation once terms are agreed.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pex_terms_redline.pdf (pdf)
